bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8; Crash State: KArchiveDirectory::addEntry / KArchive::findOrCreate / KArchive::findOrCreate; Sanitizer: address
bug_description.normalized: KraHandler::read passes attacker-controlled bytes to KZip::openArchive, which parses malformed ZIP central-directory names. A directory-style name with repeated trailing slashes yields an empty final component, but the vulnerable build only has a debug-only `Q_ASSERT(!entryName.isEmpty())`, so processing continues and `findOrCreate` is asked to materialize a nested parent path that reuses an earlier zero-size file as a directory. `findOrCreate` looks up that nested file via `rootDir()->entry(path)` but removes it from `rootDir()` instead of its actual parent, leaving a stale hash entry behind. The replacement `KArchiveDirectory` allocated for that path component is then deleted by `KArchiveDirectory::addEntry`'s duplicate-name branch, yet `findOrCreate` still returns the freed pointer. The outer recursive `findOrCreate` later dereferences that dangling `KArchiveDirectory*` in `KArchiveDirectory::addEntry`, producing the ASan heap-use-after-free READ.

source.description: Reads attacker-controlled ZIP central-directory pathname bytes from the archive stream into `bufferName`; those bytes determine the later directory/file path logic.
source.value_from: QIODevice supplied by KraHandler::read, ultimately backed by the fuzzer's `data,size` buffer via QBuffer
source.note: For the witness PoC, these bytes decode to malformed path strings containing repeated `/` separators and control-byte components, which drive the later empty-final-component and recursive `findOrCreate` path.

sink.description: Dereferences the freed `KArchiveDirectory` receiver to read `d->entries` while adding the next child component, triggering the recorded heap-use-after-free READ of size 8.
sink.note: ASan reports the crash at `src/karchive/src/karchive.cpp:836` inside `KArchiveDirectory::addEntry(KArchiveEntry*)` after the freed replacement directory pointer has been returned as `parent` by the inner `findOrCreate` call.

root_cause.description: Because `findOrCreate` previously failed to remove the nested old entry from its actual parent directory, the duplicate-name branch in `addEntry` frees the freshly allocated replacement directory. `findOrCreate` still returns that pointer to its caller, so it becomes the dangling `parent` later read at the sink.
root_cause.note: ASan's free stack points here. The freed object is the 24-byte replacement `KArchiveDirectory` allocated in `KArchive::findOrCreate` at line 497.

tainted_value_origin.description: The fuzz input is wrapped in a `QBuffer` and passed to every image handler. The harness then calls `h->read(&i)` at line 65 even if `h->canRead()` returned false, so arbitrary attacker bytes reach `KraHandler::read` and then `KZip::openArchive`.

parser_admitted.description: The KRA handler opens the attacker-controlled device as a ZIP archive. In the fuzz harness this read path is unconditional once `h->read(&i)` is called, so no successful KRA magic check is required for the malformed ZIP-like PoC to enter `KZip::openArchive`.

coarse_trace.summary: Wraps the fuzzer bytes in a `QBuffer` and calls `KraHandler::read` even if `canRead()` fails, so arbitrary input reaches the KRA ZIP parser.
Constructs `KZip` on the attacker-controlled device and enters `KZip::openArchive` to parse the bytes as a ZIP container.

Reads a malformed central-directory pathname, keeps processing even though the directory entry's final component is empty, and asks `findOrCreate` to build a nested parent path that reuses an earlier empty file as a directory.

Attempts to replace the nested empty file by a directory, removes it from the wrong directory object, then allocates a replacement `KArchiveDirectory` that `addEntry` immediately deletes as a duplicate while `findOrCreate` still returns it.
The outer recursive `findOrCreate` reuses that dangling directory pointer as `parent` and dereferences it in `d->entries.value(...)`, causing the heap-use-after-free READ.

fine_trace.note: Reads the attacker-controlled central-header filename/path bytes for the current ZIP member. In the witness PoC those bytes form malformed path strings with repeated `/` separators and control-byte components.
Decodes `bufferName` into the `QString` pathname `name`. Subsequent `endsWith('/')`, `lastIndexOf('/')`, and `QDir::cleanPath()` decisions all operate on this attacker-derived string.

This member is treated as a directory entry because `name.endsWith('/')` was true at lines 700-708, but stripping only one trailing slash still leaves the resulting `name` ending in `/`. `pos` therefore points at that final separator and `entryName` becomes empty. The only check is debug-only `Q_ASSERT(!entryName.isEmpty())`, so the ASan build continues instead of rejecting the malformed member.

Derives the nested parent path to materialize for this malformed directory member. The saved warnings and the recursive ASan stack show that this path extends beyond a previously created empty-file component `\u000F` under parent `" \u001D"`, so the parser is reusing `.../\u000F` as a directory prefix and still has another child component to add.

In the inner recursive `findOrCreate` on the reused prefix ending at `.../\u000F`, `rootDir()->entry(path)` resolves an existing zero-size file at that nested path rather than a directory. The saved warnings later identify the containing directory as `" \u001D"` and the reused child name as `"\u000F"`.

Because the existing entry is an empty file, `findOrCreate` tries to replace it with a directory. It incorrectly calls `removeEntry()` on `rootDir()` even though `myEntry` belongs to nested parent `" \u001D"`; the saved warning `directory "/" has no entry with name "\u000F"` shows this removal failed. `delete myEntry` on line 478 then frees the old file object while leaving the stale hash slot behind in the real parent directory.

Allocates a fresh replacement `KArchiveDirectory` for the reused path component `dirname = "\u000F"`. ASan's allocation stack points to this line for the 24-byte region that is later freed and then read.

When the real parent directory `" \u001D"` tries to insert the replacement directory, the duplicate-name test at lines 836-838 is true because step 6 left the stale `"\u000F"` hash entry in place. `addEntry` therefore logs `directory " \u001D" has entry "\u000F" already` and deletes `entry` (the replacement `e`). This is the ASan free context.

The outer recursive `findOrCreate` stores the inner call's return value in `parent`, but that inner call has already freed the replacement directory at step 8. Because `findOrCreate` still returns `e` after `parent->addEntry(e)`, `parent` now aliases a dangling `KArchiveDirectory*`.

The outer recursive caller now tries to add the next child component through this freed `parent`. Entering `KArchiveDirectory::addEntry`, it dereferences the freed receiver to read `d->entries`, producing the recorded ASan heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 at `src/karchive/src/karchive.cpp:836`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch only bumps kimageformats' KF5/ECM version requirements and does not modify the crashing `src/karchive` code in this workspace. No fixed-version execution is staged here, so the saved evidence does not demonstrate crash suppression from that diff alone.

poc.trigger: Feed the 163-byte PoC to `kimgio_fuzzer`. The harness wraps it in `QBuffer`, calls `KraHandler::read`, and `KZip::openArchive` parses malformed central-directory names until a repeated-trailing-slash directory member reuses the nested empty-file path `" \u001D/\u000F"` as a directory and drives the dangling-`KArchiveDirectory*` path.

format.name: Malformed ZIP/KRA-like container
format.contract: A byte stream that `KZip::openArchive` will parse as ZIP central-directory entries, with an earlier zero-size nested entry at `" \u001D/\u000F"` and a later directory-style member whose cleaned parent path extends beyond that component while its final component is empty after stripping only one trailing slash. That combination makes `findOrCreate(" \u001D/\u000F")` free a replacement directory and return it to the outer recursion.
